theCityOfFog.title: Scenario IV-A: The City of Fog

intro.title: Scenario IV-A: The City of Fog
intro.part1: You're already digging through your bag for a coat to fend off the chill of the bay air when the train screeches to a halt. You've arrived from your long trip at the Third and Townsend Railway Depot, the gateway to the beautiful city of San Francisco. The distant rumble of cable cars adds to the urban cacophony. It’s a stark contrast from the comfortable quiet of Arkham, but you're not here to take in the local flavor.
intro.part2: It isn’t hard to dig up dirt on the Tenebrarum murders. Every bit of local street gossip tells the same story—members of the Tenebrarum Lodge, a local gentlemen's club, are dropping like flies. The latest casualty is Jerry “The Cap” Lanza; co-owner of Fisherman's Wharf on paper, but in reality, a notorious whiskey baron with a rap sheet a mile long. His death has thrown his personal crew into a frenzy, and they're tearing up the streets every night, howling for bloody vengeance. It's a familiar tune that echoing the hit on Declan O’Doyle at the Hotel Seasons. If the name of the Tenebrarum Lodge wasn't enough to set your alarm bells ringing, the pattern you're seeing now sure is. It's time to find out where the Lodge itself is and see what secrets it’s hiding.
intro.part3:
A primly-dressed young woman with a smile as bright as her neatly permed hair intercepts you as you leave the station. She introduces herself as Milly Mercer, a representative of the Tenebrarum Lodge. “I'm so thrilled you answered our invitation,” she beams, collecting your luggage before you can object. You can’t help but ask how she knew you'd respond when you didn’t send word ahead. “Neopythagorean metageometry,” she replies breezily, as if such an insane answer makes any sense at all. As she escorts you along, Miss Mercer explains in rapid-fire fashion that the Tenebrarum Lodge is a brotherhood that’s welcomed in many of San Francisco's literati—Ambrose Bierce, Jack London, and George Sterling, to name a few. The motley crew of writers practices an obscure occult art called megapolisomancy, the manipulation of energy derived from the sheer mass of metropolitan cities.

The eccentric author Thibaut DeCastries presides over the lodge itself, as its current Grand Metropolitan Abbot. “Anything else you'd like to know?” she chirps cheerily as she complete her barrage of bizarre, difficult to process information. You hesitate, but succumb to temptation—you ask her about any ties between the Gentleman's Club and the mythical Mater Tenebrarum, the youngest of the Three Mothers.

Miss Mercer's grin suddenly sharpens, her teeth glinting in the light. “Oh, silly rabbit. Don't spoil the surprise so quickly, will you? You're skipping ahead.” With a crash, the bulb in a nearby streetlight bursts with a flash before plunging the street into darkness. Gasps erupt from passersby. By the time you look back, Milly Mercer has vanished.
intro.part4:
The fog rolls in thicker than pea soup as you make your way to a small café halfway between Union Square and North Beach, where Dr.

Armitage has arranged for you to meet a Professor John McGregor, a specialist in Occult Sciences at UC Berkeley. The café is a quiet spot just off of Powell street—but when you approach, something is already wrong. A pair of squad cars are parked out front, their red lights flashing. You push through the gathering crowd, and the scene inside makes your stomach churn.

McGregor’s body slumps over a table, a pool of blood spreading across the floor. Your eyes land on a crumpled napkin near McGregor’s hand, half-hidden under the table. You snatch it up, careful not to draw attention. The napkin is stained with coffee and blood, but you can make out the faint scrawl of a message: “Sorrow has come to California. Beware Mater Tenebrarum.”
intro.part5:
Anna Kaslow’s tale lingers in your thoughts as you walk through the fog-choked streets. Anna knew Mater Tenebrarum to be the true identity of Elizabeth Salmon, the proprietress of the Three Conies Inn—before she met her end at the gallows for the crime of witchcraft. But Elizabeth Salmon had been just one facet of the true Mater Tenebrarum, a splinter of her power. The fortune teller had hinted at the existence another avatar of this malevolent force, one that had made her home in the grandeur of the Elio Varelli’s Palace Hotel in San Francisco—until the devastating earthquake of 1906, when the hotel burnt to cinders.

The Three Mothers are cunning, but so are you. If a facet of Mater Tenebrarum is truly hiding somewhere in San Francisco, it's up to you to find her—before she finds you, first.
intro.part6:
A dense blanket of fog has enveloped the city by the time you exit the station. You pull your coat tighter around you—there’s something not quite right about the way the fog moves, the way it seems to curl around your feet-— something almost intentional. The clamor of urban life and the city’s famous trolleys has been muted, replaced by an oppressive silence that presses against your ears.

Somewhere in this fog-choked city, Mater Tenebrarum is waiting. You'll just have to hope you can find her before she finds you.
intro.part7: Finlay rushes up behind you, excitement and panic on his face. He’d lingered behind at the station for a moment to make a call back home, and whatever news he’d received has him on tenterhooks. “She’s here,” he blurts out, his voice a loud whisper, eyes wide with barely contained excitement. “Naomi, I mean. The boys just got word. She's here in San Francisco, somewhere. You think it’s got something to do with, uh, Mother Tannenbaum?” You nod, ignoring the way he’s butchered the pronunciation of Mater Tenebrarum’s name. The entire fate of the O’Bannion gang has been entangled with the Three Mothers’ since that bloody night at the Hotel Seasons—why should it stop there? “She's a real long way from home,” Finlay mutters, his voice straining under the anxiety. “We gotta find her, whatever it takes.”

rules.title: Fog Tokens & Locations
rules.body:
Throughout this scenario, you will be instructed to place Fog Tokens on locations. When you are instructed to do so, place a resource token (from the token bank) on the specified location as a Fog Token. A Fog Token has no inherent game effect. However, some scenario card effects may change while you are at a location with a Fog Token.

Veiled locations in The City of Fog are double-sided with story card backs, and enter play revealed. For the best experience, do not look at the reverse side of these cards.
